correctness.rationale: For a connected graph, a nonzero state fixed by the cube of synchronous three-state threshold-one Greenberg–Hastings must have every vertex advance at every step: permanently resting vertices cannot neighbor an advancing one. This is equivalent to each initial vertex having a successor-color neighbor. On the binary triangular cactus, classify each rooted subtree with fixed root phase as A (internally supported) or B (root unsupported and needing parent). For the single triangle (A0,B0)=(2,1), and an explicit nine ordered phase-pair enumeration yields A_next=5A²+6AB+2B² and B_next=4A²+4AB+B². The full root needs A and cyclic recoloring gives P_h=3A_h. The normalized logarithmic recursion gives a convergent entropy series, r_h=B_h/A_h remains in [1/2,3/4], with q(r0)=17/2 and q(rh)>10 thereafter. Hence c>(log340)/4>log(2+sqrt5), rigorously compared to the known triangular-chain transfer eigenvalue. Direct enumeration of 3^7 states at height1 and recurrence identities match. Finite-state tests do not replace the all-height polynomial recursion.
